key_terms.جَهَنَّمَ: Hell, the fire of the hereafter
key_terms.مِرْصَدًا: An ambush, a trap, or a place prepared to catch someone

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says Hell is a 'mirsad' (ambush/trap)?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Anbiya (21:96) highlights Jahannam as a 'mirsad' (ambush or prepared trap), emphasizing that Hell is not merely a passive state but an active, awaiting destination for the arrogant who reject divine guidance. This imagery reinforces the concept of divine justice, where the fate of the disbelievers is pre-ordained and ready to receive them upon their departure from the world. The term 'mirsad' also implies a strategic placement, serving as a constant reminder of the consequences of hubris in both this life and the hereafter.
